root_cause.text: The AppArmor policy unpacking function `unpack_pdb` lacks bounds checking on DFA start states (`pdb->start[0]` and `pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE]`) read from untrusted policy data, allowing out-of-bounds reads when these values are used as indices into the DFA state table in `aa_dfa_next()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that "start states are read from untrusted data and used as indexes into the DFA state tables" and that "if the start state exceeds the number of states in the DFA, this results in an out-of-bound read." The patch adds a validation check comparing the start states against `state_count = pdb->dfa->tables[YYTD_ID_BASE]->td_lolen`, rejecting policies with out-of-bounds values. The KASAN report confirms the slab-out-of-bounds read at `aa_dfa_next+0x2a1`.
